newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money steady at 11.5/12.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money steady at 11.5/12.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was steady at 11.5/12.0 percent on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity supply appeared to be sufficient on Wednesday, keeping overall rates stable. Bank Indonesia supplied only 89 billion rupiah into the market in the morning.
One- and three-month money were quoted at 12.75/13.00 and 13.50/13.75 percent, respectively. The tighter rupiah market helped improve short-term swaps.

The central bank has freshened the longer-term market by offering one-year bilateral papers (SBIs) since February. Banks seemed to have some excess rupiah reserves following a decline of 50 basis points in the weekly auction of SBIs.
The weekly auction of 100 billion rupiah SBIs to be settled on Thursday was carried out at 12.0 percent, down from 12.5 percent auctioned earlier.
The central bank offered one-week SBIs at 6.5, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
One state bank dealer said the offer of longer-term papers suggested the bank wanted to revive the longer-end market.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 11.91 percent, compared with 10.82 percent on Monday.
